title: Cosmos DB Request Units and Performance
description: Understand request units (RUs), provisioned throughput, and autoscale to optimize Cosmos DB performance and cost.

data.text: Cosmos DB does not use traditional CPU or memory metrics. Instead, it measures throughput in **Request Units (RUs)**, which represent the normalized cost of any operation — reads, writes, queries, or stored procedure execution. Understanding RUs helps you predict costs, size containers, and troubleshoot throttling.

One RU roughly equals the cost of reading a 1 KB item by its id and partition key. More complex operations like cross-partition queries consume more RUs because they touch multiple physical partitions. Writes, deletes, and stored procedures also have their own RU costs.

data.title: Typical RU Costs
data.content: Approximate RU consumption for common operations
data.code:
Read 1 KB item by id           ~1 RU
Write 1 KB item                 ~5 RUs
Query 100 results (small)       ~10-50 RUs
Query 10,000 results (large)    ~500-2,000 RUs
Stored procedure execution      Varies by logic

rows: Fixed RUs per container or database
Scales between a minimum and maximum automatically
No minimum; billed per RU consumed

data.title: Enable Autoscale with Azure CLI
data.content: Set autoscale with a maximum of 4,000 RUs
data.code:
az cosmosdb sql container throughput update \
  --account-name cosmos-demo \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --database-name AppData \
  --name Orders \
  --max-throughput 4000

data.title: Use the RU Calculator
data.text: Microsoft provides a Data Explorer tool in the Azure Portal that estimates RU costs for your queries before you run them in production. Use it early to avoid surprises.

data.title: Exercise: Measure and Optimize RU Costs
data.description: Run queries and measure their RU consumption.
steps: Create a container with 400 RU/s provisioned throughput.
Query all items and note the RU charge in the response headers.
Add a filter on the partition key and run the query again.
Compare the RU cost of the filtered query vs the unfiltered one.
data.expectedOutcome: Clear evidence that partition-aligned queries consume fewer RUs than cross-partition queries.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RUs are the universal currency of throughput in Cosmos DB.
Cross-partition queries cost more RUs than single-partition queries.
Provisioned, autoscale, and serverless throughput serve different workload patterns.
Use the Data Explorer RU calculator to estimate costs before production.
data.takeaway: Understanding RUs lets you design Cosmos DB solutions that are fast, predictable, and cost-effective.
